A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the LLAVIDAL and ADL-X research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J are readable and support comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-data comparisons, modality ablations, action-recognition and forecasting results, video-description evaluations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, multimodal-training and data-curation ablations, qualitative analyses, and a human evaluation of generated QA pairs.

M1.justification: v1 selects video plus object features after unsuccessful joint pose/object integration, leaving progressive training for future work. v2 introduces MMPro: independently initialize modality connectors, combine video and skeleton modalities, then integrate objects, with ordering guided by first-stage losses. Section 5 also describes trajectory-derived object context instead of v1's object-label list. PoseCLIP becoming SkeletonCLIP is otherwise a renaming.

E1.justification: The underlying training and evaluation datasets are retained, including the appendix fall videos. However, v2 broadens the temporal benchmark from action forecasting to temporal completion: TSU now includes identifying intermediate actions using surrounding actions and video evidence, demonstrated in Figure 13. LEMMA remains forecasting. This substantively changes a central benchmark's task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds ChatUniVi to the main comparison, an X-InstructBLIP-style alignment comparator, and a YOLO+CLIP alternative for HOI extraction. It also evaluates CogVLM+GPT, CogVLM+Llama, and BLIP2+GPT on MCQ tasks; these pipelines appeared only in v1's video-description comparison. These are substantive changes in comparator participation.

E3.justification: v2 reports switching scoring to local Llama 3.1, including mapping generated MCQ answers to options, and removes Mementos object/action F1 evaluation. It introduces curation-component controls and a human-validation protocol involving five participants, 100 sampled videos, six QA pairs per video, and a 1–5 rating scale. The stated overall training epochs, batch size, and learning rate remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's training-source and cue-representation analyses, v2 adds separate cropping, stitching, and weak-supervision ablations; human QA-quality validation; an HOI-extractor comparison; and tests of progressive modality order, modality affixes, and skeleton context within MMPro. Appendix F extends the classwise analysis to MMPro, and Figure 13 adds temporal-completion cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new human-study average is a point result, without uncertainty or inter-rater agreement reporting.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced or added. LLAVIDAL's Charades/Smarthome recognition scores change from 59.0/58.8 in v1 Table 5 to 55.2/48.1 in v2 Table 4, under changed training and scoring conditions, so these do not establish regressions. v2 adds MMPro and curation results and a human rating of 4.1/5, removes Mementos scores, and revises classwise findings. Several new Appendix F numerical statements disagree with Figure 10.

T1.justification: v2 Section 5 corrects the per-frame object-feature dimensional definition from 8n by Do in v1 Section 3.3 to n by Do, distinguishing a frame from an eight-frame trajectory. Appendix C retains the pooling and alignment-loss mathematics with renamed notation. No new proofs or theoretical guarantees are introduced.

C1.justification: MMPro becomes a central contribution in v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion, replacing v1's deferred plan for effective joint modality integration. The benchmark contribution is reframed around temporal completion and explicitly includes video description. The broad claim of state-of-the-art ADL performance is retained rather than newly introduced.

C2.justification: v1 interprets joint fusion as an unresolved optimization limitation. v2 attributes the difficulty to conflicting gradients and sparse HOI features, motivates a loss-based curriculum, and claims MMPro resolves it; the corresponding Appendix I limitation is removed. Skeleton context plus features is now interpreted as beneficial in the two-modality experiment, rather than redundant. The long-video sampling and summarization limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies equal-length MMPro stages, connector-weight initialization and transfer, and the local Llama 3.1 evaluation procedure. Most existing reproducibility information is retained, including encoder choices, feature dimensions, hardware, training hyperparameters, Appendix H prompts, and Appendix J release statements. The PDFs do not establish an actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around synchronous multimodal alignment versus X-InstructBLIP and LanguageBind, progressive training, and newer video-understanding approaches. Added works include ChatUniVi, VideoLLM-online, Language Repository, and progressive-learning research. Mementos and several earlier dataset references disappear. These changes exceed the relocation and rewriting of existing related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, related work, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten and reorganized. v2 introduces standalone related-work and background sections, separates modality construction from MMPro training, and consistently shifts pose terminology toward skeleton terminology. The title, author list, and contribution structure also change.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document to a two-column layout, redraws introductory and curation diagrams, and adds modality-extraction, MMPro, and QA/context pipeline figures. It consolidates the main benchmark tables, relocates the dataset-comparison table to the appendix, redesigns the classwise plot, and adds temporal-completion examples. Several existing appendix figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: MMPro controls directly address v1's unresolved joint-fusion limitation, while component ablations and human QA validation strengthen evidence for ADL-X's quality. These improve the paper's support for its central contributions. The net gain is limited by removal of Mementos F1 checks and new reporting inconsistencies: Appendix F conflicts with Figure 10, and Table 4 does not support universal-best claims, including Smarthome accuracy of 48.1 versus VideoLlava's 49.2.
